(1) the tone of the business model (the way it is disclosed) is significantly associated with the verifiability of disclosure; (2) the tone is significantly associated with corporate governance, performance and verifiability; (3) the verifiability is significantly associated with performance, and (4) the tone of disclosure is significantly associated to corporate governance, performance, verifiability and the tone of the financial statements.

how the tone of the disclosure affects its informativeness.
the tone of the business model disclosure and how the tone is related to the corporate governance, performance and verifiability of disclosure itself.
two main issues: (1) how the tone of BM disclosure affects the quality of the information provided and (2) whether managers manipulate this tone to achieve a desired impression on stakeholders.

the tone of the business model disclosure is not neutral, and it is not neutral because the tone of the disclosure is related to the tone of the performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in spite of its innovative features, integrated reporting does not seem to be able to overcome the limitations of current BM disclosure.
the IIRC has failed to provide a standard for BM disclosure that is not open to manipulation by management.
integrated reporting is not a panacea for the lack of BM disclosure, since it may be used by managers as an IM tool.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IIRC should consider the tone of the disclosure in the future version of their framework.
the tone of the integrated reports’ disclosures is not a neutral representation of the BMs but a strategic communication tool that managers use to influence the perceptions of the stakeholders.
the tone of BM disclosure should be carefully considered in the design of integrated reporting.
